input: Can you tell me where Float Co is located in Hong Kong and how I can get there using public transit?
expected_output: Float Co is located at Basement, 89 Caine Road, Mid-Levels, Hong Kong. You can get there by MTR: from Central station Exit D1, use the Central Midlevels escalator to Caine Road or take bus routes 12, 13, 40, 40M from Lan Kwai Fong / D'Aguilar Street to Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum / Caine Road bus stop (about 15 minutes). Alternatively, from Sai Ying Pun Exit C, walk about 15 minutes or take bus 40M, 103 to Aberdeen Street bus station, or minibus 22, 22S, 28S, 10, 31 directly outside Float Co.

input: What is the difference between preset and adjustable water temperatures during float sessions at your spa?
expected_output: The preset water temperature is designed to match skin temperature to create a sensory-deprived environment, while the adjustable temperature can be changed slightly upon request if made at least 1 day in advance to allow time for heating.

expected_output: Use React Developer Tools to inspect component trees and state in real time. Enable the Profiler early to detect performance regressions by recording interactions and analyzing render durations. Avoid leaving DevTools enabled in production unless profiling is explicitly required.

- What is React Developer Tools and why do I need it?
It’s an official browser extension that lets you inspect component trees, state, hooks, and performance data in real time—making debugging and optimisation far easier than using console.log.
- Does React Developer Tools work with React 19 features like Server Components and concurrent rendering?
Yes. Version 19 added full support for profiling concurrent transitions, Suspense boundaries, and Server Components’ streaming updates (DEV Community).
- Can I run React Developer Tools in production?
You can profile production builds by enabling the special profiling flag and embedding the <Profiler> component, but be mindful of performance overhead and security.
- How do I see why a component re-rendered?
Select the component, open the Why did this render? panel, and React Developer Tools will diff previous and next props/state to highlight triggers.
- Is React Developer Tools available for React Native apps?
Yes. Launch the dev-menu in React Native and open the DevTools page to inspect components on iOS and Android simulators.
- How do I export profiling data?
After recording, click the export icon in the Profiler to save a JSON file; upload it to React DevTools or performance dashboards later.
- What complementary tools pair well with React Developer Tools?
Redux DevTools, React Query Devtools, Apollo Client Devtools, and Chrome’s Performance panel all augment insights gathered from React Developer Tools.
- Will React Developer Tools slow down my app?
In development, minimal overhead is acceptable. In production, avoid including the DevTools backend unless profiling is explicitly required.

• Firefox: React Developer Tools - Firefox Add-ons

This tab shows all React components, props, state, and used context. For example, consider a Counter component:

```jsx
function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Clicked {count} times</button>;
}
```
It renders real-time updates in the Components tab, removing the need for console logs.

The Profiler lets you record interactions, measure render times, and detect unnecessary re-renders. Example:

• Type into a search input
• Stop and review which components were rendered and why

This helps identify performance bottlenecks efficiently.
